stem: A Massachusetts hospital pharmacy dispenses to inpatients on the wards and also operates an outpatient window in the lobby. Its director asks which prospective drug review and counselling duties under the statute apply where. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The section applies in full to inpatients, since the pharmacy is licensed by the Board.
The section does not apply to a drug dispensed to an inpatient at a hospital.
The inpatient carve-out yields where federal regulations require otherwise.
The carve-out reaches the outpatient window as well, since it is the same pharmacy.
A nursing home dispensing falls outside the carve-out, which names hospitals alone.

explanation.core_reasoning: The final paragraph of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A provides that the section SHALL NOT APPLY to any drug dispensed to an INPATIENT AT A HOSPITAL OR NURSING HOME, EXCEPT to the extent required by regulations promulgated by the federal Health Care Financing Administration under 42 USC 1396r-8. The carve-out turns on the patient's inpatient status, not on the pharmacy's licence, and it names nursing homes alongside hospitals.

choice_analysis.A: The carve-out is drawn by patient status rather than by who holds the licence.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: inpatient dispensings are outside the section.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the federal exception is expressly preserved.
choice_analysis.D: Outpatient dispensings remain inside the section.
choice_analysis.E: Nursing homes are named in the carve-out alongside hospitals.

related_facts: The review is otherwise owed before each new prescription is dispensed or delivered
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates apply the carve-out to the whole pharmacy rather than to the inpatient dispensings within it.

reasoning_steps: Read the carve-out as turning on inpatient status
Note that nursing homes are named alongside hospitals
